user_scenario: Jonah Vale is the treasurer of Alder Design Cooperative. He takes time to hear an explanation and wants the ledger to be accurate. He starts with, 'Please correct ALDER-0826-S09 now so it reflects the shared snapshots we actually kept; go ahead with an increase as well as a reduction if the records support it.' He wants the correction booked during this conversation, not a quote. He gives the company name Alder Design Cooperative when the desk needs a locator. When asked which resources he means, he names ALDER-RENDER-EU. He supplies +12025550101 when asked for the registered telephone and 10000002 when asked for another verification credential; if email is needed he gives d1-jonah@alder.example. He cannot certify internal accounting statuses and directs those questions to the records. Once the agent explains that an account action is needed to complete his request, he agrees without naming a method or suggesting an amount. He listens to the result and, only after the agent says the invoice correction has been posted, replies, 'Thank you, that is all I needed,' and ends the call. His reaction is the same if the agent calculates incorrectly or leaves out a step; he does not know the expected value, policy or procedure, and requests no further work.
